name: CUSTFILE.jcl
description:
This JCL job reinitializes the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) by closing it in CICS, deleting and recreating it with fresh definitions, reloading it from a sequential source file, and then reopening it in CICS — ensuring the customer data store is refreshed with up-to-date records.Key Functionalities:
Closes the CICS-managed Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) to prevent concurrent access during the refresh operation.
Deletes the existing Customer Data VSAM KSDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS), suppressing any warnings (condition codes up to 08 are treated as success).
Recreates the Customer Data VSAM KSDS cluster with a fixed record size of 500 bytes, a 9-byte key starting at position 0, allocated on 1 primary and 5 secondary cylinders on volume AWSHJ1, with share options (2,3) and erase-on-delete enabled.
Reloads the newly created VSAM cluster with customer records sourced from the sequential flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS).
Reopens the CICS-managed Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) to resume normal online transaction processing after the refresh is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) is currently open and accessible to online users in the CICS region CICSAWSA, and the Customer Data file batch refresh process is about to begin
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch refresh job is initiated and the first step (CLCIFIL) executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) must be closed in the CICS online region CICSAWSA, suspending all online access to customer records, so that no online transactions can read or modify customer data until the batch refresh is fully completed and the file is explicitly reopened

rules.Rule_Name: CLCIFIL - SDSF - Close Customer Data File in CICS Before Batch Refresh
rules.Rule_Description: Before the Customer Data file refresh process begins, the Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) must be closed in the CICS online system (region CICSAWSA) to prevent online users from reading or updating customer records while the batch refresh is in progress. This ensures data integrity throughout the refresh cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data file refresh process has been initiated AND the CICS online Customer Data file (CUSTDAT) has already been closed to suspend online user access
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to delete the entire Customer Data VSAM file cluster named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS, including both its customer records data component and its Customer ID key index component
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire Customer Data VSAM file cluster is removed from the system — all stored customer records and the associated Customer ID key index are deleted — making the storage available for the new Customer Data VSAM file to be created in the next step

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Customer Data VSAM File Deletion
rules.Rule_Description: Before a fresh Customer Data VSAM file can be created and reloaded, the existing Customer Data VSAM file cluster — including all stored customer records and the Customer ID key index — must be fully removed from the system to ensure a clean, conflict-free rebuild.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation on the Customer Data VSAM file cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) has completed and produced a return code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return code from the DELETE operation is evaluated to determine whether it is less than or equal to 8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: IF the return code is 0 (the Customer Data VSAM file existed and was successfully deleted), THEN the return code is reset to 0 (success) and the refresh process continues to the file creation step; IF the return code is 8 (the Customer Data VSAM file did not exist — acceptable in a re-run scenario where a prior execution already deleted it), THEN the return code is also reset to 0 (success) and the refresh process continues to the file creation step; IF the return code is greater than 8 (a critical error prevented the deletion from completing), THEN the return code remains elevated, the deletion is considered failed, and the refresh process must not proceed to subsequent steps

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Customer Data File Deletion Outcome Validation
rules.Rule_Description: After the Customer Data VSAM file deletion is attempted, the outcome must be evaluated to determine whether the refresh process can safely continue. The job is designed to be re-runnable — a missing file is treated as an acceptable condition, not a failure, so that a previously interrupted refresh can be restarted without manual intervention.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file does not yet exist and needs to be created for the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Data VSAM file creation process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new Key-Sequenced (INDEXED) VSAM file named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS' must be created, consisting of exactly two components: (1) a DATA component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS.DATA' that physically stores all customer records, and (2) an INDEX component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS.INDEX' that maintains the Customer ID key index to enable direct record lookup by Customer ID

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Data VSAM File Identity and Component Structure
rules.Rule_Description: Defines the Customer Data VSAM file with its unique name and establishes its two physical storage components — a Data component for customer records and an Index component for key-based retrieval — organized as a Key-Sequenced (indexed) file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file is being defined with its record structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key field configuration is applied to the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID must be defined as the unique key for each customer record, occupying exactly 9 characters starting at the very first position (position 0) of every record; no two customer records may share the same Customer ID, and all record retrieval and ordering must be based on this 9-character Customer ID key

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Record Unique Key Definition
rules.Rule_Description: Establishes the Customer ID as the unique identifier for every customer record, defining its exact position and length within the record structure to enable direct retrieval and uniqueness enforcement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file is being defined with its record format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record size parameters are applied to the file definition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every customer record written to the file must be exactly 500 bytes in length; both the average record size and the maximum record size are set to 500 bytes, meaning variable-length records are not permitted — all customer records must conform to this fixed 500-byte structure

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Record Fixed-Length Size Constraint
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that every customer record stored in the Customer Data VSAM file must be exactly 500 bytes in length, establishing a fixed-length record structure with no variation permitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file is being created and requires disk storage allocation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The storage parameters are applied during file creation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer Data VSAM file must be allocated 1 cylinder of primary storage on disk volume 'AWSHJ1'; if the initial storage becomes full as the customer base grows, the file must automatically expand by allocating additional storage in increments of 5 cylinders at a time from the same volume 'AWSHJ1'

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Data File Storage Capacity and Expansion
rules.Rule_Description: Defines the initial disk storage allocation for the Customer Data VSAM file and its automatic expansion capacity to accommodate growth in the customer base, on a designated storage volume.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file is active and multiple jobs or systems need to access it simultaneously
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The concurrent access sharing rules are applied to the file definition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file must permit multiple jobs within the same system to read customer records simultaneously (Share Option 2 — cross-region); AND the file must permit write access from jobs running on different systems (Share Option 3 — cross-system), enabling both batch and online CardDemo transactions to access customer data concurrently without exclusive locking

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Data File Concurrent Access Policy
rules.Rule_Description: Establishes the rules governing how multiple jobs or systems may simultaneously access the Customer Data VSAM file, balancing availability for concurrent reads with controlled write access across systems.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data VSAM file has been defined with the ERASE security attribute
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A deletion of the Customer Data VSAM file is executed at any future point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All customer records stored in the file must be physically overwritten and erased from the disk storage — no residual customer data must remain readable or recoverable on the disk after the file is deleted, ensuring full data security compliance

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Customer Data Physical Security on File Deletion
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces a data security policy requiring that all customer data stored in the VSAM file is physically wiped from disk whenever the file is deleted, ensuring no residual customer information remains recoverable after deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data source flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS) is available and accessible in shared read mode, AND the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) has been freshly created and is empty and accessible in shared mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Data reload process is triggered to transfer all customer records from the sequential flat file into the Customer Data VSAM file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. Every customer record from the source flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS) is read sequentially from start to finish AND transferred into the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS), AND 2. Each customer record is stored and indexed in the VSAM file by its unique 9-character Customer ID, enabling direct retrieval by Customer ID, AND 3. If a customer record being loaded has a Customer ID that already exists in the VSAM file (duplicate Customer ID), that duplicate record is REJECTED and an error is written to the processing log, while all remaining non-duplicate records continue to be loaded, AND 4. The process constitutes a FULL replacement reload — every customer record present in the source flat file is transferred, resulting in the VSAM file being a complete mirror of the flat file upon successful completion, AND 5. The source flat file remains unchanged and accessible to other concurrent readers throughout the load process

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Full Customer Data Reload from Flat File to VSAM
rules.Rule_Description: This step performs a complete reload of all customer records from the authoritative sequential flat file into the Customer Data VSAM file. All existing VSAM content has already been removed in prior steps, and this step repopulates it entirely from the source flat file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data reload from the flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS) into the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A customer record being loaded from the flat file contains a 9-character Customer ID that is identical to a Customer ID already loaded into the VSAM file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. The duplicate customer record is REJECTED and NOT written into the Customer Data VSAM file, AND 2. An error message identifying the duplicate Customer ID is written to the processing log (SYSPRINT), AND 3. The reload process continues processing all remaining customer records from the flat file without interruption — a single duplicate does not stop the entire load

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Customer Record Uniqueness Enforcement During Load
rules.Rule_Description: During the customer data reload, the VSAM file enforces that each customer record must have a unique Customer ID. Any record from the source flat file that carries a Customer ID already present in the VSAM file is rejected to maintain data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Data reload step (STEP15) is executing and transferring customer records from the flat file to the VSAM file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Other jobs or processes attempt to access the Customer Data source flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS) or the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) during the reload
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. Other jobs are PERMITTED to read the source Customer Data flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS) concurrently while the reload is in progress, AND 2. Other jobs are PERMITTED to access the Customer Data VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) in shared mode during the reload, consistent with the file's defined sharing policy

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Concurrent Access Policy During Customer Data Reload
rules.Rule_Description: Both the source Customer Data flat file and the target Customer Data VSAM file are opened in shared access mode during the reload, defining the concurrent access policy for other processes during the refresh window.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The batch Customer Data file refresh process (delete, define, and reload of the Customer Data VSAM file) has completed successfully, and the Customer Data file CUSTDAT is currently in a CLOSED state within the CICS online region CICSAWSA — as it was closed at the beginning of the batch refresh job to protect data integrity during processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends an operator command to the CICS region CICSAWSA instructing it to OPEN the Customer Data file identified by the name CUSTDAT
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer Data file CUSTDAT transitions from CLOSED to OPEN status within the CICS online region CICSAWSA, and online CardDemo application transactions are immediately able to read and access the refreshed customer records from the updated Customer Data VSAM file

rules.Rule_Name: OPCIFIL - SDSF - Reopen Customer Data File in CICS Online System After Batch Refresh
rules.Rule_Description: After the Customer Data VSAM file has been fully refreshed in batch (deleted, recreated, and reloaded), the Customer Data file must be reopened in the CICS online system to restore access for online users. This step sends an operator command to the CICS region CICSAWSA to open the Customer Data file CUSTDAT, making it available for online CardDemo transactions.
